name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
grip: Neutral throughout, with palms facing each other and thumbs toward the upper dumbbell heads.
description: Curl two dumbbells while maintaining a neutral hand position, with the upper arms close to the sides.
setup: Stand with a dumbbell beside each thigh, palms facing inward.
Keep a small knee bend, straight wrists and shoulders relaxed.
instructions: Flex both elbows to bring the dumbbells toward the fronts of the shoulders.
Keep the palms facing each other rather than rotating them upward.
Keep the upper arms and torso steady.
Lower the dumbbells under control to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Rocking backward or lifting the elbows far forward.

logging.example: Two 12 kg dumbbells: record 12 kg per dumbbell.
logging.note: Keep the same exercise variant and record each dumbbell's mass rather than the combined pair.

variantNote: Standing simultaneous neutral-grip curl. Alternating and cross-body versions differ in timing or arm path.
reviewNotes: Both arms are illustrated together; use separate side records if logging alternating repetitions.
Muscle roles are qualitative; the exercise still trains the biceps.

sources.title: ACE - Hammer Curl
sources.scope: Standing dumbbell hammer curl and neutral hand position; anatomical role ordering is editorial.

illustration.alt: Two black-and-white drawings of a standing hammer curl with palms facing inward throughout.
